incident-bot: Pager triggered -> service=runtime-inference-eastus severity=page action=trigger reason=latency_p99>1.2s across /v1/generate :rotating_light:
pagerduty: PagerDuty incident #PD-84921 fired and routed to Priya (on-call). Remember to acknowledge in PD or the bot will escalate in 5m.
Priya (on-call): acked in PD. I'm looking at dashboards — p99 for generate has jumped to ~1.5s from normal 0.12s. p95 at 0.45s.
Priya (on-call): initial check: error budget showing 4.3% burn over last 10m for tenant-scoped SLOs. High burst from eastus-az2.
Ben (sre): thanks — any recent deploys or autoscale flaps?
Priya (on-call): no deploys in last 30m. autoscaler shows scale-up attempts, several pods OOMKilled in the last 8m. Logs show "KV cache memory exceeded, evicting entries" repeatedly.
Ava (eng): that matches a model rollout we did earlier; candidate-quantized-v2 was pushed to a subset of nodes in eastus-az2 for canary. Could be memory pattern differences.
Sam (product): customer impact? are requests failing or just slow?
Priya (on-call): 99.3% of requests are OK; tail is slow. No increase in 5xxs, just latency. Some customers on interactive endpoints are reporting sluggishness (support tickets 3421, 3423).
Priya (on-call): mitigation plan I'm trying now: 1) pin routing away from canary nodes, 2) scale dedicated serving pool + warm KV cache, 3) if that fails fallback to cpu-quantized variant.
runtime-bot: Routing rule update queued: move 30% traffic off eastus-az2 canary nodes -> in-progress.
Priya (on-call): running quick query to check pod mem usage:```\nkubectl top pods -n runtime | grep eastus
```
Priya (on-call): seeing two pods at 96% mem; one at 99% then OOMKilled.
Ben (sre): do the OOMs correlate with prefix-heavy requests? check logs for "prefix_cache_write" spikes.
Priya (on-call): grep shows many prefix_cache_write spikes. Looks like a hotspot of requests hammering a small subset of keys -> hot-KV behavior.
Ava (eng): can we enable KV eviction backpressure or increase per-pod mem limit temporarily? I can push a config bump to increase pod memory by +4Gi for the group.
Ben (sre): do that as short lived remedial. Also open autoscaler window to allow faster scale-up. Priya, can you throttle client-side rate for the most aggressive tenants?
Priya (on-call): starting config bump via rollout canary override:```\napiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  kv_cache_max_entries: "200000"
  kv_eviction_backpressure: "true"
```
Priya (on-call): applying now. runtime-bot: config apply completed on 3/4 nodes.
runtime-bot: autoscaler: minReplicas increased from 6 -> 10 for pool runtime-eastus-canary.
Priya (on-call): p99 down to ~1.1s after routing shift and mem bump. Still above SLO but trending.
Sam (product): good — are we going to roll back the canary?
Ava (eng): recommend pausing canary rollout and draining canary nodes for now. I'll queue a rollback of candidate-quantized-v2 to previous stable for eastus.
Priya (on-call): queued rollback; draining nodes started. Expect traffic normalization in ~4-6 minutes.
Ben (sre): documenting action items: 1) pause canary, 2) increase kv_cache_limits, 3) temporary autoscaler bump, 4) follow-up postmortem and perf regression test for candidate-quantized-v2.
Priya (on-call): noting customer impact: interactive latency increased for ~3% of users for ~15m window. Noted support tickets + product alerts.
Sam (product): will notify affected account owners and draft status update.
Priya (on-call): on-call handoff in 45m to Ben. leaving a summary in PD. If things re-escalate, PD will auto-escalate to Ben in 5m.
Ben (sre): taking over at handoff. Priya great triage. I'll follow up on postmortem action item owners and schedule perf regression runs for quantized variants.
Priya (on-call): thanks — closing thread once metrics stabilize. Current p99 ~0.48s and trending toward baseline. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident PD-84921 status -> acknowledged -> mitigated -> monitoring.
